scope: Candidate 1.2.0 keeps supported XSLT 4.0 node union patterns as one template rule, using the highest default priority of their alternatives even when a lower-priority alternative is the one that matches. xsl:next-match visits that rule once, and overlapping alternatives do not create competing rule identities. Earlier effective profiles retain separate rules and their original per-alternative next-match behavior. Explicit priorities remain unchanged. Priority calculation recognizes pipe and union keyword operators, recursively computes nested alternatives, and preserves strings, predicates and EQName URIs; parenthesized 4.0 matching retains the declaring static namespace/type context. Empty top-level alternatives are rejected with XTSE0340. Twenty-eight regressions verify maximum priority, single visits, duplicate alternatives, failing ambiguity modes, nested/default namespaces, explicit priorities, version overrides, delimiters and invalid alternatives. Native next-match (including si-next-match) remains 46/8/6, and type-alias remains 22/10/0 with all prior wildcard/type-pattern gains retained. Four next-match 4.0 assertions (021a/023a/025a/039a) reference version-2.0 stylesheets and therefore still select the earlier effective profile; their fixtures and assertions remain unchanged. Processor-level selection for those lower-version native fixtures is a separate harness/API boundary. Other node-pattern priority forms, broader pattern grammar, schema-defined atomic priorities, named-type/fixed-namespace authoring contexts, non-template type registries, remaining record/result cases and annotated function types remain follow-ups. N04/N05 and REQ-126 remain In Progress. Published version remains 1.1.3; candidate 1.2.0 remains unpublished.
